headline: Monday: both books went 0 for 7 on closes since last night (RAIN -72.9% was the worst), nothing cleared the ticket gate after 10 AM, and the clearest lesson is to move a kill line up to entry once a paper gain is big, because RAIN and PIERRE both gave back large gains within an hour.
learned: Big paper gains disappeared within an hour. RAIN (Solada, opened 10 AM at L3, 44.9k ADA) marked +57.9% at 12:15 PM after graduating, was -13.4% by the 12:40 PM pulse and closed at -72.9% at 1:08 PM (12.2k ADA, holders 72 -> 59) on net selling into a ~12k ADA pool. PIERRE (Pump.fun) marked +28.1% at 10:15 AM, was -27.4% by 11:30 AM and closed at -42.3% at its kill line. Both kill lines sat too far below the high.

Fresh graduates open on thin pools. Solada curves graduate with about 10.3k ADA, so RAIN, DEXY and HIVE all started under the ~11k side where a few wallets move price. DEXY bounced three times (64.9k -> 97.1k -> 126.7k ADA) and SER ran 58.3k -> 145.9k, and both faded by 9 PM (DEXY 106.8k with 78 holders, SER 109.2k with 77). Not opening either of them was right.

The Solana-side hunt found no real traction. MISS bonded on pump.fun around 3:20 PM after a 93% -> 99% curve run with natives rising 18 -> 38, but natives fell 38 -> 29 -> 24 -> 21 within about 90 minutes as the post-bond hours were sell-led (h1 10 buys / 26 sells at 5 PM), and it hit its kill line. No Solana-side paper snipe opened, because rule q's 50 natives was never met, so there is nothing to grade. CORE sat at a 72.8% curve with 28 natives all evening.

Swarm keys win on timing, not shape. Across BRO, DEXY, IAGONE, GUINEA and BESSTIVE, the 28 swarm round trips that entered within 15 minutes of go-live won 25 times (median hold 19 minutes), while the 18 later entries won 7 times. A 100-ADA paper ticket checked every few hours can't copy that.
pulse_caught_early: RAIN's collapse: the 12:40 PM pulse had it below entry and the 1:08 PM pulse closed the ticket, nearly an hour before the 2 PM desk run.
DEXY on its graduation (first seen at the 12:40 PM pulse), before the 2 PM run.
MISS's curve push to 99% with natives 18 -> 38 at the 3:10 PM pulse, before it bonded and before the 4 PM run.

SER's rebound (holders 74 -> 87, 58.3k -> 124.1k ADA) at 5:15 PM and DEXY's 126.7k peak at 8:13 PM, both of which faded by the 9 PM run. The pulse spots pops quickly, so rule y now makes single-pulse pops wait.
adapted: Solada rule z (new tonight): once a ticket on a pool with under ~15k ADA side marks +50%, its kill line moves up to entry. RAIN would have closed near -13% instead of -72.9%.
Pump.fun rule pf-u (new tonight, mirrors solada:z): the same move to entry after a +25% mark. PIERRE would have closed near -27% instead of -42.3%.

Rules added during today's runs: Solada u (confirm an ADA-side kill caused by an LP pull on the next pulse), v (fresh graduates stay L2 for about 3 hours until the side is 15k+), w (pump.fun bonds shed natives; Solana-side names stay L2 for 2 hours after bonding), x (swarm entries after 15 minutes add nothing) and y (thin-pool rebounds need two pulses of holder growth with the side rising); Pump.fun pf-r, pf-s and pf-t; and day reviews for both books.

Thresholds moved: rule v caps fresh graduates at L2, and rule w adds a 2-hour post-bond wait on top of rule q's 50 natives. pf-r would loosen pf-m to a 1% cumulative holder drop on 5,000+ holder coins only if two more pf-m exits recover the way Dacity did.
Tomorrow the lean schedule starts: desk runs at 10 AM, 2 PM and 7 PM, and the hourly pulse comes back for 9 AM to 9 PM only once a ticket opens, which is also when rules z and pf-u need marks.

scoreboard.verdict: Pump.fun's exit signals held up better today: its holder-drop exits closed Dacity at -16.8% and UHI at -25.3%, while Solada's one entry signal, RAIN's curve re-hold, lost 72.9%. Neither launchpad produced a winning entry.

asks: The Solana forensics pull request (#6) is tested green and still waiting for a merge. Merging it lets workflow runs trace Solana holder funding, which replaces yesterday's request for a Birdeye or Solscan key.
